title: Product members
summary: Diceroll → Settings → Members as Kenji Mori, a Diceroll admin, sees it right after inviting Marco for Commerce only: Diceroll's own admins (direct, from a rule, and the new invite), then the people who manage Diceroll through a platform-wide role, read-only.
compare: The sidebar is Diceroll's product context only; Kenji holds no platform role, so the context switcher lists Diceroll alone and no Platform page (Home, Members, Settings…) appears anywhere.

Members is a tab of the product Settings hub (Features, Presentation, Keys and secrets, Members), with Settings active at the foot of the sidebar; until ST-08's hub lands it is a standalone page with the same content.

The first table ('Admins') lists Diceroll's own bindings: Kenji (You), Lucía from the diceroll-store SSO rule, and marco@example.com as an invite. The role column shows the Diceroll binding only, never the person's roles in other products.

A binding that comes from an SSO rule (Lucía) has a menu, drawn in Other states: 'Add areas…' makes a direct binding on top of the rule's role, limited to the areas the viewer holds; 'Remove from Diceroll' is locked and names the rule and the Superadmins who can change it.
'Platform roles' lists Superadmins and All-products admins read-only with their source (Root rule, SSO rule) and no menu.

Invite people (the same button words as Platform → Members) opens the same drawer with the role fixed to Product admin, the product fixed to Diceroll, and only the areas Kenji holds selectable (no escalation).
The success toast (Other states) says 'Invited marco@example.com' with Undo, which removes the binding. It never guesses a name from the address.

Phone: both tables become stacked rows (person and menu, then the role tag, its areas on the next line, and the source indented under the name); the Settings tab strip fades at its scrolled edge instead of clipping a word, and the toast sits clear of section headings.

designReview.reviewer: UX designer (visual critique of rendered screenshots)
designReview.verdict: Fix applied: a rule-given role now has Add areas…, so the no-access page's promise holds; copy and phone polish done.

findings.issue: Lucía's rule-given row ends in 'Set by a rule' with no action, so Kenji can't add Licensing for her, which breaks the no-access page's promise.
findings.resolution: Lucía's row has a menu, drawn open on desktop: 'Add areas…' (a direct binding that adds to the rule's role, limited to the areas Kenji holds) and a locked 'Remove from Diceroll' whose note names the diceroll-store rule and the Superadmins who can change it (Ada Lindqvist, Jonas Weber).

findings.issue: 'Add people' here vs 'Invite people' on Platform → Members for the same drawer; the toast guesses 'Marco' from the address.
findings.resolution: The button is 'Invite people'. The toast reads 'Diceroll admin for Commerce. We emailed marco@example.com and told every Superadmin.'

findings.issue: On phone the tab strip shows a clipped 's' from 'Features', and the toast covers the 'Also manage Diceroll' heading.
findings.resolution: The tab strip fades over its first 40px, so the scrolled edge reads as more tabs rather than a fragment. On phone the toast sits over the new invite's row, clear of the heading (measured at 360 and 390: toast 660–760 px, heading at 788 px).

findings.issue: The open row menu and the toast covered data in the primary shot, and the active Members tab was clipped to 'Membe' on phone.
findings.resolution: The menu and the toast moved to Other states; the tab strip scrolls the active tab into view (.tabs.follow-active) with the right-edge fade; at wide the two cards share one height.

findings.issue: The product name appeared three times and who can change a role was stated twice.
findings.resolution: Cards are 'Admins' and 'Platform roles', the column is 'Role'; the first subtitle is dropped; the toast is 'Invited marco@example.com' with Undo; the names of who can change a role live in the row menu only.

findings.issue: Tables stretched to about 1615px at 1920, so cells sat 275px or more apart and the page widths differed across the area.
findings.resolution: Pages cap at one content width, centred: 1280px for tables, 1136px for forms and status pages (kit .page.cap-table, .page.cap-form).

findings.issue: Small muted mono keys, dates and helper text carried facts at subtle colour and under 12px; disabled buttons were near invisible; row-menu targets were 28px.
findings.resolution: Fact-bearing small text moves to the muted token and 12px or more; the light subtle token is #4f586d (4.5:1 or better on every surface in both themes); disabled buttons keep a visible border at 0.6 opacity (0.8 on primary); the row-menu trigger is 32px with a 44px hit area (44px on phone); colour-only Adds and Joins carry a glyph.

findings.issue: Other states left 120 to 700px of dead space beside shorter cards, and the captions narrated layout.
findings.resolution: Other states sit on one equal-width grid (3 columns from desktop, 2 on tablet, 1 on phone) with the page's card primitive; captions name the state and its trigger.

findings.issue: Change the Members tab count to 6, or drop it.
findings.resolution: declined: The count is existing data and structure. Revisit it in copy review if it is judged ambiguous.

findings.issue: h1 plus tabs is the kit's pattern; role names and the glossary are owner and consolidation-plan decisions.
findings.resolution: declined: Change the h1 to match each tab, add breadcrumbs on platform pages, or add 'Rename Console access to Viewer' and a glossary entry.
